# Trellis AI guidance for Svelte browser apps

Directory avatarUrl is a Trellis-hosted image-only bearer lasting at most ten
minutes. Do not log it. Render with referrerpolicy="no-referrer" and local initials
on missing/broken images; reread the authorized directory to renew an expired URL.
The browser never needs to contact Gravatar or an identity-provider image host.

Use the guide from the same Trellis revision as the installed libraries. This
guide describes the optional Trellis Svelte integration. Trellis does not
require Svelte, a UI design system, a configuration parser, or a particular
application architecture.

Use this file for AI coding agents working in a Svelte or SvelteKit browser app
repository that consumes Trellis. The language-neutral guide is:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oats-center/trellis/main/docs/static/llms-full.txt

The TypeScript service guide is:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oats-center/trellis/main/docs/static/llms-typescript.txt

## Browser app setup

Author the app in `contract.trellis`, run `trellis generate`, and pass its
generated participant module to the Svelte integration. Set `[package]` and a
package `name`, here `dashboard-trellis`, in `trellis.toml`. Install the resulting
ordinary ESM package through your application's package manager.

```ts
import {
  createTrellisApp,
  type TrellisClientFor,
} from "@oatscenter/trellis-svelte";
import { participants } from "dashboard-trellis";

const participant = participants.acmeDashboard.participant;

type AppClient = TrellisClientFor<typeof participant>;

export const trellisApp = createTrellisApp({
  participant,
  trellisUrl: "https://localhost:3000",
});
```

Trellis integration behavior:

- `createTrellisApp(...)`, `TrellisProvider`, `SvelteTrellisConnection`, and
  browser client auth mode `"browser"` are the intended browser-app wiring.
- Browser sign-in is OAuth Authorization Code with PKCE and DPoP against the
  installation's dedicated OAuth origin. Local-password or OIDC sign-in and
  explicit capability consent happen on Trellis's own portal at that origin.
  Application code never renders Trellis login or consent, handles upstream
  provider callbacks, or constructs grant sets or capability lists.
- Let `TrellisProvider` and `BrowserOAuthClient` from
  `@oatscenter/trellis/auth/browser` own the redirect, callback, token exchange,
  and refresh. Connected control uses generated APIs over NATS; do not call
  Trellis HTTP endpoints directly or add HTTP context, logout, or bootstrap
  calls. This does not restrict unrelated application HTTP APIs.
- Browser custody lives in the `trellis-oauth` IndexedDB database: a
  non-extractable DPoP key and an encrypted refresh credential scoped to the
  selected installation and app. Ephemeral runtime keys, signed authority,
  grants, transports, and issuer keys remain in memory.
- Use `OwnAuthorityController` only when UI needs a reactive view of the SDK's
  verified authority. It does not own refresh or verification; do not implement
  a second verifier in Svelte or TypeScript code because Rust/WASM is
  authoritative.
- Issuer trust comes from the selected OAuth origin and authenticated rotation
  links. Pending devices poll `/auth/device/enroll` through the device
  activation helpers; approved devices connect with a signed provisioned
  admission in NATS CONNECT, never an HTTP bootstrap.
- `TrellisClientFor<typeof participant>` and `createTrellisApp(...)` consume the
  generated participant directly. Do not reconstruct participant evidence in
  application code.
- Keep generated API SDKs and browser auth helpers on their explicit subpaths or
  local workspace aliases.

## Svelte integration

Mount the app owner with `TrellisProvider` near the Svelte app root, then read
the typed client with `trellisApp.getTrellis()` and connection status with
`trellisApp.getConnection()`. The connection accessor returns a Svelte-reactive
`SvelteTrellisConnection`.

Keep this logical app owner across automatic transport handoffs. Equal-policy
renewal keeps a healthy socket; newly approved authority is adopted on a ready
successor without a manual refresh method or upgrade flag. Do not recreate the
client or add an effect that reconnects it on each authorization refresh. Safe
accepted work continues on its receiving connection. While own authorization
coverage is unavailable, fresh calls either wait within their acquisition budget
or report unavailability.

Use Svelte context, not module-global mutable state, for app-scoped Trellis
clients. `@oatscenter/trellis-svelte` owns the app context created by
`createTrellisApp(...)`.

## Cross-participant clients

For calls to another API, declare the narrow required or optional `use`
selection in `contract.trellis`. Generated participant types expose only those
selections.

For labels of other Trellis users, select and obtain consent to `usersRead`,
then use `Auth.Users.List/Get` for active directory profiles. For owner edits,
select `accountProfileWrite` and call generated `usersProfileUpdate` with the
self account's `profileRevision` and an idempotency key. Omitted fields stay
unchanged; explicit clears restore linked-provider defaults, and manually set
email is unverified. Manual choices survive later OIDC login. `Users.Resolve`
with `accountRead` is self-only. Ordinary profiles omit `account`; admin details
require delegated and currently held `trellis.auth.v1:users.manage`. A directory match
does not grant access to application-owned records; key those rules by immutable
`principalId`, not names or email.

```trellis
app Dashboard {
  implements "acme.dashboard@v1";
  use orders {
    call rpc "Orders.Get";
  }
}
```

## Vite, npm, and `svelte-check`

Native generation does not execute TypeScript or require a Vite plugin. The
application's bundler and type checker still need to resolve imports from the
one generated package and the installed Trellis packages. Its executable `.js`
and `.d.ts` require no consumer transpilation or Trellis CLI once packaged. Keep
generated implementations out of Git and run `trellis install` before local builds.
Use the
resolver configuration appropriate to that application; the checked-in app demo
illustrates one npm/Vite setup, not a required frontend stack.

When an import fails, inspect its actual generated specifier and the installed
package exports. Regenerate stale code rather than editing generated imports.
Type the connected client with `TrellisClientFor<typeof participant>`; an extra
API SDK is not needed just to type the app client.

## Verification

Use the format, typecheck, lint, test, run, and migration commands configured by
the app repository. If contract artifacts or generated SDKs changed, run
`trellis generate` and commit `trellis.lock`; `.trellis` output remains
disposable.
